title: Vegetation: Introduction, types of vegetation in Nepal
topicTitle: Vegetation: Introduction, types of vegetation in Nepal
notes: Vegetation is the plant cover of a place, set by temperature, rain, soil and height. Nepal's cover changes quickly because the land rises from the Terai to the high Himalaya.
Below about 1000 m the belt is tropical. Sal, Shorea robusta, dominates, with sisau along rivers. This is the Terai and the inner Terai.
From about 1000 to 2000 m the belt is subtropical. Chir pine, Pinus roxburghii, and Schima–Castanopsis forest are the markers.
From about 2000 to 3000 m the belt is temperate. Oak and Rhododendron arboreum, the national flower, are the markers. Rhododendron here is a flowering plant.
Toward 4000 m, fir, birch and juniper thin out. The timberline is the last trees. Above it, alpine herbs and grasses continue until the snowline, which is higher.

Forest and other wooded land cover about 45 percent of Nepal. The east is wetter than the west at the same height, so the species lists differ. Community forestry is a management success in the middle hills, not itself a belt.
